requirement:
The harness MUST expose a `habeas` tool accepting exactly one of these request
forms. Each form MUST correspond to one existing evidence-input kind:

| Request fields | Evidence input returned | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file: String`, `line_start: Integer`, optional `line_end: Integer` | Outline inputs for the innermost outline nodes covering the range | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `file: String`, `item: String` | Outline input | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `requirements: String` | Requirements input, including its matching names | {cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs` |
| `definition: String` | Definition input | {cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs` |

Selector arguments MUST use the syntax defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Reads MUST use the current
project working tree, including unstaged changes to tracked files and staged new
files. By default, source inputs MUST stay within the project root after
resolving symlinks; in a Git worktree, both the requested file and its resolved
target MUST be present in the Git index. Projects outside Git MUST use the same
containment rules without requiring an index. Failure to read an existing
repository's index MUST be reported as an error.
The project-root `evidence/` directory MUST be excluded from model reads by
default, including symlink aliases. Every source the harness supplies to the
model MUST be redacted under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. Generated build outputs MUST follow
{cite}`requirements.authoring.generated_inputs`. Workspace path overrides MUST
follow {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`, including explicit
permission for otherwise excluded inputs. A denied mandatory input MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`, and a denied model
read MUST return a tool error under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.

Line numbers are only a way to request sources; recorded evidence MUST identify
sources by outline selector and structural hash, never by line number. Request
line numbers MUST be one-based and inclusive, and omitting `line_end` MUST read
through EOF. A line-range request MUST be resolved to the innermost outline
nodes covering the requested lines, which are `line` nodes in a file using the
plain-text profile; the result MUST show the model each node's selector and
source text, without line numbers, and the harness MUST record those nodes as
outline inputs. The model-facing tool description MUST include the argument conventions
from the cited requirements, including outline selector syntax, definition
selections, and full definition names, with a short request example for each form.

A successful call MUST return the requested evidence input, populated by the
harness with the selected source text, using the existing evidence schema.
{cite}`requirements.ci.schema`
Required terminology dependencies MUST be returned alongside it as additional
definition inputs under {cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`.
The result MUST have this shape:

```text
HabeasResult {
    input: EvidenceInput,
    definitions: Array<DefinitionInput>,
}
```

`definitions` MUST be empty when no additional terminology is required. The
harness MUST record inputs supplied to the model in the assessment's evidence.
A failed read MUST add no evidence input. Access-policy denials MUST be handled
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`; other failed reads MUST return
an explanatory tool error.
rationale:
I found no gap. The code carries out each obligation and each has a test.

**Implementation map**
- **Request forms.** `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[read]` accepts exactly one of the four forms. It calls `check_keys` to reject mixed, unknown or incomplete argument sets.
  - The `file` + `item` form and the `requirements` and `definition` forms go through `AssessmentSources::read_selector` and `source_input` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs`.
  - The line-range form goes through `AssessmentSources::read_lines`. It resolves the range with `nodes_for_range` and returns the innermost nodes. An omitted `line_end` reads through EOF, and `line_start` of 0 is rejected.
  - `src/inputs.rs#fn[outline_inputs_for_lines]` produces the recorded outline inputs for line ranges.
- **Access policy.** `source_input` and `parse_file` call `SourceAccess::file` for the requested path, for every resolved range file, and for requirements and definition files. That one check carries the Git-index, containment, symlink-target, `evidence/` exclusion, generated-output, and allow/disallow rules. A denial surfaces as an error.
- **Denial handling.**
  - A model read that is denied becomes a tool error in `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]`. `pending` is extended only on `Ok`, so a failed read adds no evidence input.
  - A denied mandatory input aborts in `AssessmentSources::prepare`, which propagates the error with `?`.
- **Result shape.** `read` returns `{input, definitions}` for the single-input forms. `additional_definitions` supplies the transitive terminology via `definition_inputs`. `definitions` is empty when none is needed. The line-range form returns `{inputs, definitions}`, because the table calls for outline inputs for several nodes. I do not treat this as a conflict with the `HabeasResult` shape.
- **Recording.**
  - `record_inputs` stores the file, selector and hash only, never text or line numbers.
  - `converse` records inputs only after a successful response.
- **Tool description.** `fn[definitions]` gives the `habeas` description. It covers the request forms, one-based inclusive lines, EOF behaviour, selector syntax with percent-encoding, definition selections, full names, and a short example per form.
- **Redaction.** Redaction of mandatory inputs, reads and searches is verified by `model_inputs_reads_searches_and_citation_prompts_are_redacted`.

**Tests**
- `habeas_tool_describes_its_argument_conventions_with_an_example_per_form` covers the tool description.
- `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` covers:
  - recording of selector and hash only;
  - terminology returned alongside the input;
  - an omitted `line_end` reading through EOF;
  - bad line ranges, a missing item, and incomplete, mixed or unknown forms.
- `line_range_reads_record_the_innermost_covering_nodes` covers the innermost-node resolution and the recorded form.
- `requirements_reads_select_requirements_and_examples_but_not_definitions` covers the `requirements` form, its `matches`, and the empty `definitions`.
- `git_tools_allow_staged_and_dirty_sources_but_hide_untracked_files` and `git_symlink_reads_require_both_the_alias_and_target_to_be_tracked` cover working-tree reads and the Git-index checks.
- `nested_project_uses_only_its_part_of_the_git_index`, `empty_git_directory_in_an_ancestor_does_not_make_a_project_a_worktree` and `outside_symlinks_are_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery` cover projects outside Git and project containment.
- `unreadable_git_index_does_not_fall_back_to_untracked_access` and `invalid_git_configuration_does_not_fall_back_to_untracked_access` cover the index-read failure error.
- `generated_evidence_is_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery` covers the `evidence/` exclusion, including symlink aliases.
- `cargo_output_is_discovered_and_read_without_building_or_allowing_other_target_files` and `inherited_out_dir_is_ignored_and_metadata_failure_preserves_ordinary_reads` cover generated inputs.
- `explicit_allow_overrides_defaults_but_disallow_wins_for_alias_targets` and `allowed_ignored_and_external_sources_are_discoverable_but_disallowed_descendants_are_not` cover the explicit allow and disallow rules.
- `unpermitted_requests_outside_the_project_are_recoverable_tool_errors` covers recoverable read failures.
- `mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms` covers the mandatory-input abort.
- `explicit_untracked_reads_return_an_untracked_error_and_the_assessment_continues` in `tests/authoring_cli.rs` covers the denied-read tool error and the assessment continuing.
- `bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools` in `tests/authoring_cli.rs` covers an end-to-end line-range read and the recorded inputs.

All reachable code is covered by the `prepare`, `converse` and `outline_inputs_for_lines` impl roots. I saw no unspecified behavior and no `{fixme}` acknowledgments.

| Request fields | Evidence input returned | Definition |
| `file: String`, `line_start: Integer`, optional `line_end: Integer` | Outline inputs for the innermost outline nodes covering the range | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `file: String`, `item: String` | Outline input | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `requirements: String` | Requirements input, including its matching names | {cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs` |
| `definition: String` | Definition input | {cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs` |

default, including symlink aliases. Every source the harness supplies to the
model MUST be redacted under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. Generated build outputs MUST follow
{cite}`requirements.authoring.generated_inputs`. Workspace path overrides MUST
follow {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`, including explicit
permission for otherwise excluded inputs. A denied mandatory input MUST abort

read MUST return a tool error under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.

The result MUST have this shape:
```text
HabeasResult {
input: EvidenceInput,
definitions: Array<DefinitionInput>,
`definitions` MUST be empty when no additional terminology is required. The
harness MUST record inputs supplied to the model in the assessment's evidence.
A failed read MUST add no evidence input. Access-policy denials MUST be handled
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`; other failed reads MUST return
an explanatory tool error.
:::{req} outline_inputs
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. It MUST derive the node's
inclusive line range, including attached comments and attributes, during
validation for display and reference coverage. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, unsupported language, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
:::{req} requirements_inputs

For a requirements input, `requirements` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`, and Habeas MUST match it against all defined requirements and named examples. It MUST recompute the matches during validation, sort their full names, and compare them with `matches`. It MUST take each match's complete raw fenced declaration, including its opening and closing lines, concatenate those declarations in full-name order with one blank line between them, and compare the resulting raw lines with `text`. It MUST retain every match's current source file and inclusive line range for display and reference coverage. A selection matching no definitions MUST be invalid. Adding, removing, renaming, or changing a matched definition MUST invalidate the stored input; moving an unchanged declaration within the book MUST NOT. Errors MUST identify the selection and affected definitions when available.
:::{req} inputs

Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.
:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} redaction
Every source text the harness supplies to a model, including mandatory inputs,
`habeas` reads, and `ripgrep` results, and every source text Habeas displays in
the book or `habeas info`, MUST be redacted:
1. In a workspace `habeas.toml` or user configuration file, the value of every
explicit credential field defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.credentials`
MUST be replaced. Such a file that is not valid TOML MUST be replaced whole,
with `configuration` as the kind, because its fields cannot be located.
2. In every source, each match of a built-in rule of the `secretshape` crate MUST
be replaced. The replaced region MUST be extended through each adjacent region
that the crate's entropy heuristic flags and that only whitespace separates
from the region, repeating until no flagged region is adjacent. The heuristic
MUST NOT cause redaction on its own.
A replacement MUST read `[REDACTED:<kind>]`, where `<kind>` is the credential
field or the rule's name, and MUST keep every line break within the replaced
text, so line numbers are unchanged. Outlines MUST be built from the original
source, and the structural hash MUST hash each text piece that overlaps a
redacted region in its redacted form, so evidence never depends on a credential's
value and redaction never changes or breaks a file's outline. The `secretshape` version MUST be pinned exactly; upgrading
it MAY change redaction and hashes and MUST be treated as a deliberate change.
:::{req} generated_inputs
Habeas MUST permit existing Cargo build-script output directories as an exception
to default Git tracking and containment restrictions. It MUST discover the Cargo
build directory using metadata and inspect existing build-script output records,
without running a build or executing build scripts. It MUST NOT treat its own
inherited `OUT_DIR` environment variable as the workspace's output directory.
Only discovered output directories and their contents MUST receive this default
permission; unrelated build artifacts MUST remain subject to ordinary rules.
Workspace disallow entries MUST override this permission.
Discovery MUST tolerate missing builds or unavailable metadata; callers MUST be
able to allow undiscovered outputs explicitly using `habeas.toml`. The model's
root directory listing MUST expose available generated-output directories,
including external ones. Generated inputs MUST use outline inputs and receive
ordinary freshness checks. Validation MUST NOT
invoke a build to materialize an input.
:::{req} evidence_paths
The workspace `[evidence]` table MUST serialize EvidenceConfig. `allow` and
`disallow` MUST be arrays of nonempty literal paths, each naming a file or a
directory subtree. Relative paths MUST resolve from the selected `habeas.toml`
directory; absolute paths MUST be supported. These paths are not glob patterns.
An omitted `allow` or `disallow` MUST mean an empty array, and an absent
`[evidence]` table MUST mean both are empty, so only the default source-access
rules apply. No operation requires the section. The table has no user-file
counterpart, and these rules have no invocation options. This section refines
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections` for the evidence feature.
For authoring reads, a matching disallow MUST reject the path; otherwise a
matching allow MUST permit it; otherwise the default source-access rules MUST
apply. Explicit allow MUST override every default, including Git tracking,
project containment, generated-evidence exclusion, and automatic generated-output
rules. Disallow MUST win even when an allow or generated-output rule also matches.
Both the requested path and its resolved symlink target MUST be checked for
disallow, so an allowed alias cannot expose a disallowed target.
The same explicit disallow rules and external-path exceptions MUST apply when
resolving recorded evidence inputs, including ordinary validation. Validation MUST
remain independent of Git index membership: it
checks the recorded inputs' existence and contents. Loading path policy MUST NOT
resolve credentials or validate unused authoring settings.
:::{req} read_denial.mandatory
When source-access policy denies a mandatory input, the assessment MUST abort
before any model request and report the denied path and reason to its caller;
for an untracked file, the report MUST say what {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.untracked`
says. The aborted assessment MUST NOT write evidence or emit evidence JSON, and
its usage record MUST identify the failure. In a batch, other assessments MUST
continue, including queued assessments, and their successful writes MUST be
retained; the command MUST return a nonzero exit status after the batch
finishes.
:::{req} read_denial
When source-access policy denies a path that a model tool call names
explicitly, the harness MUST return a tool error naming the path and the reason
it cannot be read, add no evidence input, and continue the assessment.
Discovery and search MAY omit denied candidates without an error. Malformed tool
arguments and ordinary read failures MUST also return explanatory tool errors.
:::{req} schema

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, `references`, and `inputs`. `references` MUST be the reference-set digest defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input MUST have exactly one of three forms: an outline input with `file`, `item`, and `hash`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST resolve to permitted inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.input_containment`. Project-local paths SHOULD be recorded relative to the project for portability; absolute and parent-relative paths MAY be used when their resolved targets are permitted. `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, `hash` MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings. Evidence MUST NOT store source text for outline inputs.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
